slots.purpose: Weighing uses a few named measures, each a simple question, and a speech picks the two or three it wins.
slots.diagram_spec: Five equal rounded tiles in one row, each with a bold name, a small plain icon above it, and a short question below. Left to right: "Magnitude: how big?" (icon: a large and a small circle), "Probability: how likely?" (icon: a short chain of three links), "Timeframe: how soon?" (icon: a clock face), "Reversibility: can it be undone?" (icon: a curved return arrow), "Scope: who, and how widely?" (icon: a group of three dots). Under the row, one centred line: "Pick the two or three where you win, then compare directly." Ink #16191d outlines, white tiles, light grey #e1e4e8 icon fills. No blue or red.
slots.alt: Five labelled tiles: magnitude, probability, timeframe, reversibility and scope, each with its question, and a note to pick two or three.
slots.caption: The main weighing measures, each as a simple question.

slots.after_heading: Big and unlikely vs small and likely
slots.purpose: The most common weighing fight is a huge but unlikely harm against a smaller but sure one.
slots.subject: A simple two-pan balance scale. On the left pan sits a very large block drawn only as a dashed outline with a pale fill, so it looks uncertain, almost not there. On the right pan sits a small solid block, fully filled. The beam is exactly level.
slots.composition: The balance stands in the centre on a plain base. The large dashed block on the left pan rises high above its pan; the small solid block on the right is compact. The level beam shows the two can weigh the same. Nothing else in the picture.
slots.colors: The balance is ink #16191d outlines with white fill. The large block has a dashed mid grey #7d8690 outline and a very light grey #e1e4e8 fill. The small block is solid ink #16191d. No blue or red.
slots.avoid: No legal or court scales, no gavel, no explosions or bombs drawn on the block, no numbers.
slots.alt: A balance holds a huge faint dashed block and a small solid block, level: a big but unlikely harm can weigh the same as a small, sure one.
slots.caption: Big but unlikely, or small but sure? The debaters must say which counts more.

slots.purpose: Turns case means one side's harm causes or worsens the other side's: the neg's impact knocks down the aff's case.
slots.subject: A ball rolling down a straight ramp on the left. At the bottom of the ramp, on the right, stands a small tower of four stacked blocks. The ball has just reached the bottom and the top block of the tower is starting to tip over.
slots.composition: The ramp slopes down from the upper left to the middle of the frame. The ball is at the foot of the ramp, touching the tower's base. The tower stands right of centre on a thin ground line, its top block tilted. Clear left-to-right cause and effect.
slots.colors: The ball and ramp are neg red #f2232d: the neg's disadvantage. The tower blocks are aff blue #0055b8: the aff's case. Outlines are ink #16191d. The ground line is light grey #cfd4da.
slots.avoid: No people, no explosion or debris, no motion streaks or speed lines.
slots.alt: A red ball rolls down a ramp into a blue tower of blocks, which starts to tip: the neg's impact can make the aff's own harm worse.
slots.caption: Turns case: one side's impact knocks into the other side's case.

slots.purpose: When neither side puts any reason on the scale, presumption decides, and most judges start with the neg.
slots.subject: A simple two-pan balance scale with both pans completely empty. The beam is level, because nothing is on either pan. A small plain neg red marker, like a short flat tab, rests on the base of the scale on the right side, below the right pan.
slots.composition: The balance stands alone in the centre on a plain base, seen straight on. The beam is perfectly level and calm. The small marker sits low on the right side of the base, so it does not touch or press on any pan. Lots of white space around it. Nothing on the pans, nothing else in the picture.
slots.colors: Both pans, the beam, the post and the base are white with ink #16191d outlines. The only colour is the small marker on the right (the neg side), in neg red #f2232d, showing the usual neg default. No blue.
slots.avoid: No weights, coins or blocks on the pans, no tilt of the beam, no court scales or gavel, no people.
slots.alt: An empty, level balance with a small red marker at the base on the neg side: with no reason on either side, most judges give presumption to the neg.
slots.caption: With nothing on the scale, it stays level; most judges then start with the negative.

slots.purpose: Judges decide rounds in different ways, and each brings a different tool to the same round.
slots.subject: Three simple faceless figures sitting side by side behind one long plain desk. Each holds up a different simple object: the left figure a clipboard with a column of plain check boxes, the middle figure a small two-pan balance, the right figure a completely blank white card.
slots.composition: The desk runs across the lower middle of the frame. The three figures are evenly spaced behind it, facing the viewer. Each object is held at chest height so it reads clearly. Nothing on the wall behind them.
slots.colors: Figures are mixed flat greys (#e1e4e8, #cfd4da, #7d8690) with black outlines. The desk and objects are white with black outlines. The check boxes are empty squares. No blue or red.
slots.avoid: No faces, no gavel, no robes, no judge's bench or courtroom, no writing on the clipboard or card.
slots.alt: Three judges at one desk hold a checklist, a balance and a blank card: stock issues, policymaker and tabula rasa judges decide differently.
slots.caption: Same round, different judges, different tools.

slots.purpose: A short, honest paradigm helps debaters more than a long essay.
slots.subject: On a plain desk surface, one small index card with four plain straight lines and a simple pen lying beside it. Pushed back and to the side is a tall, thick stack of loose paper sheets.
slots.composition: The small card is in front, slightly left of centre, large in the frame, with the pen angled beside it. The tall paper stack is behind and to the right, less prominent but fully visible. Simple flat desk line.
slots.colors: The card is white with a black outline and four black straight lines. The pen is ink #16191d. The paper stack is light grey #e1e4e8 with black outlines. No blue or red.
slots.avoid: No writing, scribbles or wavy text lines on any paper; the paper stack shows only its edges.
slots.alt: A small card with four lines sits in front of a tall stack of paper: a few honest lines make a better paradigm than a long essay.
slots.caption: A few honest lines beat a long essay.

slots.after_heading: Step 3: Adjust the parts you control
slots.purpose: Adapting means the speaker adjusts how they speak to fit the listener, not what is true.
slots.subject: On the left, a simple faceless standing speaker figure turning a large round dial knob mounted on a small stand. On the right, a seated judge figure at a small desk, writing on a clipboard. The speaker's head is turned toward the judge.
slots.composition: Speaker and dial on the left third, judge and desk on the right third, both on one thin ground line, with open space between them. The dial is large and simple so the action of turning it reads clearly.
slots.colors: Figures are mixed flat greys (#cfd4da, #7d8690) with black outlines. The dial is white with a black outline and one short black pointer line; no tick marks or numbers. The clipboard is white with plain straight lines. No blue or red.
slots.avoid: No faces, no microphone, no speech bubbles, no numbers or marks around the dial.
slots.alt: A speaker turns a dial while watching a judge write: adapting means adjusting speed and style so this judge can follow, not changing the truth.
slots.caption: Adjust how you speak to the judge in front of you.

slots.purpose: The last rebuttals narrow many arguments down to the one or two that win.
slots.subject: A wide plain funnel. Many small blank cards pour into its wide top. Only two cards come out of its narrow spout at the bottom.
slots.composition: The funnel is centred, wide end up. About ten small cards are scattered just above and inside the wide top. The two cards that come out sit just below the spout, clearly separate and slightly larger. Plenty of white space around.
slots.colors: The funnel is white with a black outline. The many incoming cards are light grey #e1e4e8 with black outlines. The two cards that come out are white with thick black outlines. No blue or red.
slots.avoid: No writing on the cards, no hands, no liquid, no sparkles around the two cards.
slots.alt: Many cards go into a funnel and only two come out: a good 2NR or 2AR picks the one or two arguments that win.
slots.caption: Going for everything usually means winning nothing.
